purpose: Canakinumab is used to treat certain rare inflammatory conditions, including a group of diseases called periodic fever syndromes, systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (a type of childhood arthritis), and adult-onset Still's disease. It helps reduce painful flares of inflammation and improve quality of life for people with these conditions.
how_it_works: Your immune system produces a protein called interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) that causes inflammation. In some people, too much of this protein is made, leading to ongoing pain, swelling, and fever. Canakinumab works like a targeted blocker — it attaches to IL-1β and stops it from triggering that harmful inflammation, helping your body calm down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include infections (like colds, runny nose, or respiratory infections), injection site reactions (redness or swelling where the shot is given), headache, stomach pain, nausea, and feeling generally tired or unwell.
warnings: Because this medicine calms part of your immune system, you are more likely to get serious infections. Tell your doctor right away if you have signs of infection like fever, chills, or cough. Do not take it if you have an active infection. You should not receive live vaccines while on this medication. It may also worsen conditions like tuberculosis (TB), so your doctor will test for TB before starting treatment.
typical_dosing: Canakinumab is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous). The dose and how often you receive it depends on your condition, your weight, and your age. For many conditions, it is given once every 4 to 8 weeks. Your doctor or nurse will give you the injection, or teach you how to give it yourself at home.
